parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression; foreign passports are ordinarily accepted, no bathroom/facility ban, no police sweeps or organised targeting of trans people documented. Current negatives are real but bounded: border-guard stops of male-marker holders under martial law (a documented, current, state-run exposure that outs or detains gender-marker-mismatched travellers), unresolved mobilisation-exemption status, and psychiatric/diagnostic gatekeeping affecting document changes. Protections are partial — employment and media anti-discrimination in force, but no gender-identity hate-crime aggravation, and the rule-of-law roadmap items are unconfirmed. Violence evidence is dated (2011–2013 incidents with weak police response), so it is weak evidence about the present, and acceptance is documented as rising (70.4% 2024 support for equal rights). Hostile family/Civil Code provisions are resident-facing. This sits near the 0.65 tier — lawful, generally serviceable, with a genuine border-level exposure and incomplete remedy.
